prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one transparent cutout sprite for an existing top-down 2D antique card-game HTML tabletop.
Create ONE anatomically coherent human LEFT hand with a small length of clothed forearm, viewed directly from above, showing the BACK of the hand. It belongs to an opponent seated beyond the TOP edge of the table. The forearm enters from the upper-right/top edge and the hand reaches diagonally DOWN AND LEFT toward the center of the table. The index and middle fingers extend naturally close together toward the lower-left, as though gently releasing the upper-right corner of a playing card just placed on the table. The remaining fingers are relaxed and softly curled, thumb natural. Exactly five anatomically plausible digits, a single hand and wrist.
COMPOSITION: portrait cutout, sleeve crosses the top edge of the image (never a detached closed sleeve end). Wrist around the upper middle/right; fingertips near the lower-left quarter. Show just enough forearm to connect to an off-screen seated person. Leave transparent space around the side and finger contour. No playing card in this asset; the fingers will be composited on a real HTML card.
STYLE: finely painted 2D dark-fantasy tabletop illustration, delicate brown ink contours, restrained etched hatching, softly painted parchment-warm skin. Elegant tactile materials, consistent with ornate burgundy-and-antique-gold cards. Not photorealistic, not a 3D render. Natural hand proportions, not monstrous. Mature alchemist's hand with small restrained reddish-brown reagent stains on two fingertips, no wounds.
COSTUME: dark burgundy woven sleeve, black-brown aged leather cuff, one small antique-gold clasp, a narrow worn brass ring. Muted dark burgundy #4a1724, antique gold #ac8c4e, black-brown #261a15; warm tan skin, restrained highlights.
LIGHT: soft warm light from upper-left, own shaded volume but no large baked floor shadow; contact shadows will be added in HTML.
BACKGROUND: genuinely transparent alpha. ONLY the hand, cuff and sleeve. No table, no cards, no vial, no person portrait, no frame, no text, no watermark. The downward-left reach and the top-edge sleeve origin must clearly read as an opponent reaching from the far side of a table.
